content: Clean tweets do not contain vulgar or offensive language. We noticed that some tweets have some offensive words, but the whole tweet should not be considered as offensive due to the intention of users. This suggests that normal string match without considering contexts will fail in some cases. Examples of such ambiguous cases include: Humor, ex: يا عدوة الفرحة ههه> (“yA Edwp AlfrHp hhh” – “O enemy of happiness hahaha”); Advice, ex: لا تقل لصاحبك يا خنزير> (“lA tql lSAHbk yA xnzyr” – “don't say to your friend: You are a pig”); Condition, ex: إذا عارضتهم يقولون يا عميل> (“A*A EArDthm yqwlwn yA Emyl” – “if you disagree with them they will say: You are an agent”); Condemnation, ex: لماذا نسب بقول: يا بقرة؟> (“lmA*A nsb bqwl: yA bqrp?” – “Why do we insult others by saying: O cow?”); Self offense, ex: تعبت من لساني القذر> (“tEbt mn lsAny Alq*r” – “I am tired of my dirty tongue”); Non-human target, ex: يا بنت المجنونة يا كورة> (“yA bnt Almjnwnp yA kwrp” – “O daughter of the crazy one O football”); and Quotation from a movies or a story, ex: تاني يا زكي! تاني يا فاشل> (“tAny yA zky! tAny yA fA$l” – “again O Zaky! again O loser”). For other ambiguous cases, the annotator searched Twitter to find how actual users used expressions.
